title: Getting started with bayome
text: question microbiome differs patients Crohn’s disease (CD) ulcerative colitis (UC) controls, exposure diagnosis. Antibiotic use, age sequencing depth (reads) adjustment covariates. Repeated samples participant handled random intercept, (1 | participant_id). formula uses lme4 notation; bm_inla_formula() shows bayome translates INLA, without fitting anything: dysbiosis score HMP2 metadata used: computed microbiome , closer outcome covariate.
code: form <- ~ diagnosis + antibiotics + age + reads + (1 | participant_id) bm_inla_formula(form, meta) #> <bm_inla_model> #> INLA formula: #>   y ~ 1 + diagnosis + antibiotics + age + reads + f(.bm_re_participant_id, model = "iid", hyper = .bm_hyper$random)

title: Getting started with bayome
text: default model (shrinkage = "joint") fits species parts one INLA model. exposure (diagnosisUC diagnosisCD): prevalence (presence/absence, samples): logistic model, species estimated data; abundance (log2 relative abundance, samples species present): linear model whose species effects linked prevalence effects, u_A = lambda * u_P + e, share common prior. adjustment covariates get one effect per species part, fixed, weakly informative prior, add hyperparameters. model six: lambda spread e CD UC, variance participant effect part. residual variances, one per species, estimated outside INLA variational updates ("vb"). Continuous covariates (age, reads) standardised, abundance effects compared median across species (compositional correction), associations selected Benjamini–Hochberg 2·lfsr. fit$results holds results table, output gets all_results.tsv significant_results.tsv. read saved results: fit took 4.8 minutes laptop 4 threads.
code: set.seed(1) fit <- bayome(   input_data     = taxa,   input_metadata = meta,   output         = "hmp2_bayome",   formula        = form,   exposure       = "diagnosis",   normalization  = "TSS",   transform      = "LOG",   cores          = 4 ) res <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "HMP2_bayome_results.tsv",                               package = "bayome")) info <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "HMP2_bayome_lambda.tsv",                                package = "bayome"))

text: plot functions take bayome fit results table, return ggplot object can modified saved ggplot2::ggsave(). Overview. bm_plot_summary() shows effects top species every coefficient, selected associations marked: exposure coefficient plot left (default fit; results table name coefficients) adjustment covariates heatmap:  Effects intervals. bm_plot_effects() shows one coefficient parts, 95% credible intervals:  data behind association. bm_plot_association() shows, one species one variable, share samples species present abundance present. fit uses fit$data fit$metadata; build log2 table raw data:

what: The link between prevalence and abundance
title: Getting started with bayome
text: model estimates one link lambda per exposure coefficient: much abundance effects follow prevalence effects across species. lambda near 0 two parts unrelated abundance part reduces hierarchical model; lambda > 0, species become less frequent also tend become less abundant present. bm_plot_link() shows prevalence abundance effects species one coefficient. fit, estimated lambda appears subtitle; fit$lambda holds .  species non-zero samples, abundance effect borrows prevalence effect lambda, instead shrunk towards zero.
code: info[, c("name", "lambda")] #>          name    lambda #> 1 diagnosisUC 0.2785170 #> 2 diagnosisCD 0.2908058 bm_plot_link(res, "diagnosisCD")

title: Getting started with bayome
text: selection sets posterior probabilities become q-values, separately coefficient: "bh_lfsr" (default): Benjamini–Hochberg 2·lfsr; "rope": posterior probability effect practically null, P(|effect| ≤ rope_delta), rope_delta = 0.5 default; "lfsr": running mean sorted lfsr. rule changes q-values, posteriors, can compared saved lfsr. diagnosisCD abundance: running-mean rule selects : species without effect lfsr behaves like one-sided p-value, averaging lfsr values lets . default controls false discovery rate.
code: d <- res[res$name == "diagnosisCD" & res$model == "abundance" &            is.na(res$error), ] c(bh_lfsr = sum(p.adjust(pmin(2 * d$lfsr, 1), "BH") <= 0.1),   lfsr = sum(bm_qvalue(d$lfsr) <= 0.1)) #> bh_lfsr    lfsr  #>       3      63

title: Bayesian Occurrence-Abundance Microbiome Estimation
text: BAYesian Occurrence–abundance Microbiome Estimation bayome finds associations microbial features (taxa, genes, pathways) sample metadata. feature models occurrence (presence/absence) abundance together, links abundance effects occurrence effects, shares information across features, features observations still get stable estimates honest intervals. Every model fitted integrated nested Laplace approximation (R-INLA). arguments, formulas output columns follow MaAsLin3, existing MaAsLin3 analysis runs changing function name. Website worked example: https://jmartinez-minaya.github.io/bayome/ Status: early development (version 0.0.0.9000). default model (shrinkage = "joint") default selection rule (selection = "bh_lfsr") work tested simulated data, yet real data.

title: Bayesian Occurrence-Abundance Microbiome Estimation
text: feature j sample , Yij normalised abundance: Prevalence (samples): logit P(Yij > 0) = xi’ βjprev + random effects Abundance (samples feature present): log2Yij = xi’ βjabun + random effects + εij parts fitted together one INLA call, binomial Gaussian likelihood. Pre-processing: normalise (TSS, CLR NONE), filter, transform (LOG, PLOG NONE). Continuous covariates standardised default.

title: Bayesian Occurrence-Abundance Microbiome Estimation
text: features parts go one INLA model. model distinguishes exposure (exposure = "diagnosis": variable interest; default first variable formula) adjustment covariates (others). exposure coefficient k (example diagnosisCD), effect feature j split : Prevalence: βjkP = μkP + ujkP, ujkP ~ N(0, 2.5²) fixed: feature estimated presence data, without pooling. Abundance: βjkA = μkA + λk · ujkP + ejk, ejk ~ N(0, 1/τk) shared across features. λk one number per exposure coefficient, estimated features: much abundance tends follow prevalence data. feature non-zero samples abundance effect shrunk towards prevalence effect suggests, instead towards zero. prevalence abundance unrelated, λk ≈ 0 model reduces independent hierarchical abundance model. adjustment covariate l (example age antibiotic use) gets one effect per feature part, γjl ~ N(0, 2.5²) fixed prior: pooling, link extra hyperparameters. model two hyperparameters per exposure coefficient (λk τk) plus variances random effects, however many adjustment covariates . give every covariate full structure, list exposure. Random effects formula (example (1 | subject)) get one copy per part, replicated per feature shared variance. Residual variances one per feature, estimated "vb" (variational updates common prior). abundance effects compared median features (compositional correction). estimated λ values printed fit stored fit$lambda. alternatives shrinkage = "hierarchical" (part separately, common prior ) shrinkage = "none" (feature ). Priors set bm_prior():

title: Bayesian Occurrence-Abundance Microbiome Estimation
text: relative abundances (TSS), features truly increase, others appear decrease. abundance coefficient therefore compared median coefficient across features instead zero (median_comparison_abundance = TRUE, default). bayome posterior. coefficient posterior draw s: m(s) = median features j βj(s) δj(s) = βj(s) − m(s) lfsr, prob_positive q-values refer δ, whose posterior includes uncertainty median. coef keeps raw coefficient unless subtract_median = TRUE. null_hypothesis reports median used. Draws random: call set.seed() first reproducible results.

text: input_data Feature table (data frame matrix). Samples may rows columns; matched input_metadata name. input_metadata Metadata data frame samples rows. output Output directory all_results.tsv significant_results.tsv, NULL write nothing. formula One-sided formula string MaAsLin3 notation, e.g. ~ diagnosis + age + ordered(stage) + (1 | subject). fixed_effects, random_effects, group_effects, ordered_effects, strata_effects Alternative formula, maaslin3(). Ignored formula given. reference Reference levels, maaslin3(), e.g. "diagnosis,nonIBD" c("diagnosis,nonIBD", "site,"). min_abundance, min_prevalence, max_prevalence, zero_threshold, min_variance Feature filtering thresholds, maaslin3(). max_significance Threshold qval_individual / qval_joint significant_results.tsv. normalization, transform Pre-processing, maaslin3(). standardize Z-score continuous metadata used fixed effects. evaluate_only NULL (parts), "abundance" "prevalence". prior Priors, see bm_prior(). link "none" (separate random effects per part) "shared" (abundance random intercepts scaled copy prevalence ones). shrinkage information shared across features two parts: "joint" (default): one INLA model parts features. Prevalence: one effect per feature, u_P ~ N(0, 2.5^2) (fixed, pooling). Abundance: u_A = lambda * u_P + e, lambda (one per covariate, N(0, 1) prior) links abundance prevalence e ~ N(0, 1/tau) shared across features (PC prior tau). structure used exposure ; covariates (adjustment covariates) get one effect per feature part fixed N(0, 2.5^2) prior (see bm_prior(adjustment_sd = )): pooling, link extra hyperparameters. Formula random effects get one copy per part, replicated per feature. Residual variances "vb"; compositional reference: median features, joint posterior samples. Features without presences absences enter abundance part. evaluate_only, "hierarchical" used instead. support ordered() yet. "none": feature , median comparison posterior draws compositionality.
